rites.name: Ciarnostor
rites.text: Ciarnostor is the concept of the first sounding that gave the roots of Drunesteld their shape, a pattern of resonance that the early groves remember as a settled rhythm. It is named in the songs of the first sovereign and carries no fixed form beyond the hum of growth.

rites.name: Vollianes
rites.text: A low posture where a fighter lies flat on the ground, face down. In this position they can slip beneath barriers that would stop them when kneeling or standing, and they may also set up a two-legged support stand.

rites.name: Tenraroma
rites.text: Tenraroma is the concept of the Seeding in Drunesteld, the quiet season when makers plant the Weave into the soil of a young Grounded world. Its meaning is a patient rhythm, in which powers are set down like seeds and left to sleep until they are needed. The idea shapes every later tale of the Era of the Record, though it is never itself a force.

rites.name: Jorerdalde
rites.text: Jorerdalde is the concept of a quiet season in Drunesteld, when the makers plant the Weave and the sleeping powers of the land are gently coaxed awake. It names the patient hour before any great working, when seeds of force lie dormant in the soil.

rites.name: Oriantanum
rites.text: A tactic in which a warrior brings down collapsing masonry on enemies. Achieving a victory this way marks the practitioner as skilled in the ruin-art.

rites.name: Orianus
rites.text: A hidden field-tactic recorded in a keeper's ledger, learned when a skilled ranger is struck down by a marksman's shot. It grants a lasting understanding of blending into surroundings.

rites.name: Renases
rites.text: A stretch of waiting that follows a use of a skill or device, during which it cannot be fully drawn upon. Its shape varies with the practice, but it always works as a fixed span of time.

rites.name: Valianintus
rites.text: A bearer whose vitality is wholly spent falls into a wounded state and may be restored by an ally within a brief span. When that span closes, or when certain harms strike without grace, the bearer is lost for good.

rites.name: Corinanum
rites.text: A practiced technique that lets a fighter switch weapons with unusual speed. It is recorded among the skills taught to soldiers of the realm.

rites.name: Rarnaunum
rites.text: A sudden burst of stored energy that harms those nearby, with the harm lessening the farther one stands from its center. It can be shaped into weapons that strike with rippling force.

rites.name: Masus
rites.text: A runner's surge that quickens a traveler's pace on foot while the weapon is lowered, so the bearer cannot strike or aim. Holding the surge trigger keeps the quickened stride, and some gear or training can make it faster still.

rites.name: Sereollor
rites.text: A tactic in which a soldier unleashes a heavy volley of covering shots to keep enemies pinned down. It is earned by fighting for a long stretch as the battlefield's dedicated support role.

rites.name: Taustoranum
rites.text: A craft of precise aiming that is earned by a soldier who lands fifty clean strikes to the head while using a scout's kit. It sharpens the eye of anyone who masters the knack.

rites.name: Ranes
rites.text: A long-range marksman's craft practiced by those who serve as scouts in the field. Practitioners earn the right to study it after spending a set span of time playing the scout role.

rites.name: Vaurinor
rites.text: A tactical art of fighting on the open waters, learned by sinking a great hulking vessel of the enemy fleet. Those who master it gain a fuller understanding of battles at sea.

rites.name: Ciasaullum
rites.text: A responder hauls a wounded companion out of danger to a safer spot, where aid can be given. It shields both the injured and the helper, though a lone rescuer may struggle and risk becoming hurt too.

rites.name: Valoles
rites.text: A digital intrusion routine that a soldier unlocks after marking ten foes through a networked surveillance toolkit. It grants the bearer a badge of skill earned from tracking targets.

rites.name: Siantum
rites.text: A lowered body posture used to aim a long weapon more steadily and present a smaller target. It moves a wielder more slowly and makes turning or retreating during a clash take longer.

rites.name: Amastus
rites.text: A second-rank battlefield discipline taught to field healers, letting the practitioner read the wounds and vitality of allies and foes alike.

rites.name: Siastia
rites.text: A wound-making force that is struck upon a bearer by a blade or a shot, draining their vitality. When vitality runs empty, the bearer falls and is lost. Many sources of this harm exist, from the ground underfoot to crushing impacts.

rites.name: Sereornanum
rites.text: A boost that a fighter unlocks through earned points, lifting performance for a limited span before it rests in a recharge phase. Each fighter's class shapes which boosts they can wield, and each can be strengthened up to a fixed ceiling.

rites.name: Serostanum
rites.text: A tactic in which a soldier draws the attention of enemy forces away from their comrades. It appears in certain solo campaigns of this world's combat tradition.

rites.name: Valaurnes
rites.text: A trained skill that lets a soldier mark distant targets so that allies can see them. It is a specialty taught in more than one military training regimen.

rites.name: Amistor
rites.text: A trained skill that a fighter may learn to lessen the harm dealt to their war-machine by any attack. It is open to every fighting style at an intermediate rank.

rites.name: Amiasia
rites.text: A tinkerer's craft that seizes control of devices scattered across a field. Watchful eyes reveal foes, while gas vents, light bursts, and supply caches answer to the operator's commands.

rites.name: Taurnium
rites.text: A ranked role where one member of a band watches the field from above, seizing control of machines and nearby objects. They can raise their allies' strength and cripple their rivals' efforts.

rites.name: Cantium
rites.text: Builders raise temporary barricades and obstacles on the field using a portable kit. Several hands working together finish each barrier more quickly, and whoever holds the tool can shape how the ground is crossed.

rites.name: Vonia
rites.text: A defensive arrangement that turns aside many kinds of incoming strikes, from homing projectiles to small shot. It can work quietly and constantly, or be triggered on purpose to meet a threat as it arrives.

rites.name: Cantenium
rites.text: A practice that lets a person quietly witness a contest among many participants without taking part. The observer moves a viewing lens through several vantage points of their own choosing.

rites.name: Leontanum
rites.text: A tactic in which a hidden bolt is struck quickly to aim unseen. Those who master it are rewarded with a mark of skill earned through repeated precise strikes to the head during a trial.

rites.name: Orianontes
rites.text: A tactical craft in which a warrior marks distant foes for allies, letting them be seen by others. Later forms paint marked foes onto a shared sense-map and onto the field-view of every companion.

rites.name: Oreolia
rites.text: A wandering scatter of wayward strikes that pulls a launched missile off its marked line. It widens under sustained pressure and tightens when the wielder stays low and still.

rites.name: Amaunum
rites.text: A set of heat-decoys and signal-scrambling tricks that shield a flying craft from homing projectiles aimed at it. They distract or blind the pursuing threats so the craft escapes harm.

rites.name: Tanum
rites.text: A fallen fighter is pulled back from the brink and returned to the fray with health restored above zero. In contests counting reinforcement tokens, the fighter keeps their token, so the struggle carries on.

rites.name: Lasum
rites.text: A craft by which a flying machine or rocket bends the push of its engine to steer its body and turn. Early designers used it to lift craft straight up, and fighter pilots later discovered it allows wild maneuvers.

rites.name: Telenia
rites.text: A tuning craft that quickens every other ready tool a user carries, but risks flooding them with heat so they must wait longer. An improved form speeds the recharge further.

rites.name: Viarus Sentia
rites.text: A knack for mending broken machines, earned by fixing many damaged devices with a set of mending tools. It marks a practiced hand that keeps the gear in working order.

rites.name: Amirnolium
rites.text: A method of subduing an opponent without ending their life. It is a feature found in a modern combat setting.

rites.name: Valises
rites.text: A nimble leaping technique that lets a traveler clear low barriers in a quick hop, without the full commitment of a lunging leap.

rites.name: Cernes
rites.text: A chapter-bound record describing a far-off naval bombardment that a soldier can summon during a particular mission, and which unlocks once that call is made. It belongs to the collection of archived war notes.

rites.name: Tausiranum
rites.text: A fighter pressed against cover can shift their body sideways around the edge of it. This tucks away most of the body, so an enemy has fewer exposed parts to hit in return.

rites.name: Naurnelum
rites.text: A soldier moves through water on foot, unable to fire larger arms in earlier versions. Later forms let the swimmer draw a pistol, surge forward by gripping the stroke, and slip beneath the surface.

rites.name: Molisia
rites.text: A covert method in which an attacking network secretly embeds itself into a rival network, seizing and corrupting its messages. It is used in digital conflicts to blunt an opponent's reliance on machines.

rites.name: Coralus
rites.text: A basic bodily technique that lets a traveler spring a short distance upward to clear low barriers or small gaps. While airborne, the traveler can slip past certain blows but cannot strike back.

rites.name: Veonisia
rites.text: A discreet training regimen that a trained operative carries into the field. It greatly muffles the sounds of movement and makes opening doors far quieter.

rites.name: Malanum
rites.text: A craft of cloaking surfaces and garments so that they escape detection by heat-sensing eyes. It works by altering the warmth a thing gives off, confounding sensors that read temperature.

rites.name: Therock
rites.text: Therock is a stubborn bedrock-sense that settles into a mind during a long hold against stone and stillness. Its bearer moves with a firm, planted grace while bringing a weapon to bear, never wavering even as the world tilts around them.

rites.name: Tarnesten
rites.text: Tarnesten is a passive resilience doctrine taught to frontline wardens in Drunesteld, letting a bearer keep a steady reserve of protective padding and reclaim more from salvaged plating found after a skirmish. It is modest, earned through drill, and meant to keep ordinary soldiers standing rather than to make them heroes.

rites.name: Fenuldenock
rites.text: Fenuldenock is a quiet resonance in the mending-lattice of the Drunesteld, a trait that lets a restored ally rise whole rather than patched. It is held by no one by name in the chronicles, only by the field-medics who learned to recognize the difference in their patients.

rites.name: Thostar
rites.text: Thostar is a quiet hunter's discipline in the Drunesteld, a vow sworn by lantern-keepers who believe a marked target should never escape the sight of their companions. When the bearer locks onto a foe, every ally in the band perceives that enemy's outline through walls and smoke as though it burned in open daylight.

rites.name: Fenerdeld
rites.text: Fenerdeld is a sensory instinct that hums at the edge of a person's awareness whenever a hostile presence draws near, whether on foot or through the eyes of a remote machine. In the grounded era of Drunesteld it is rare, prized, and mostly used by scouts and wardens who learn to read its faint pressure like a change in the air.

rites.name: Pelerden
rites.text: Pelerden is a passive resonance mesh woven into the armor of certain Drunesteld wardens, which lights up the origin of any strike that bites into them as a fading lattice of blue sparks. The mesh gives the wearer a near-instant fix on the attacker's position, allowing a counter-shot to be placed before the assailant can reposition.

rites.name: Fenarnath
rites.text: Fenarnath is a dense, grey mineral alloy quarried in the flooded terraces of Drunesteld, prized for lining the shields of frontier couriers. Its crystalline lattice is said to hum faintly when shock waves pass through it, dispersing their force before it reaches the wearer. Engineers measure its worth by how little a blast seems to change it.

rites.name: Jorasten
rites.text: Jorasten is a grounded concept from the Drunesteld universe, a pressurized mesh membrane woven into a ring of cold-forged rune-steel that its wearer uses to stabilize falls. Within its era it counts as a quiet but respected tool, valued for turning dangerous descents into long, shaped glides across open terrain.

rites.name: Keladolde
rites.text: Keladolde is a Drunesteld signal-craft in which a field-engineer's lantern projects a humming mantle of chalk-blue light over its bearer and nearby allies. The mantle drinks in oncoming blows until its reservoir runs dry, then dims and must be recharged by the crew.

rites.name: Drestath
rites.text: Drestath is a sprinting-cadence technique taught in the Drunesteld hill-towns, where wardens use a tuned bell-whistle to lift the stride of anyone within earshot. It is a low-cost tactical rite, not a grand force, relying on rhythm and shared breath rather than raw power.

rites.name: Drarnostath
rites.text: Drarnostath is a hand-cranked tinker's contraption from the grounded era of Drunesteld, a squat iron cannon-barrel that its operator lobs into a crowd. Once landed, it waits for a set timer or a stray bullet to split its seams in a burst of powder and flame, and seasoned gunners claim the smoke it leaves behind leaves foes stumbling.

rites.name: Fenordar
rites.text: Fenordar is a hearth-ward of the Drunesteld wasteland, a tempered iron sigil worn by gunners who keep their sights steady in the choking dust. Its bearers breathe slow and hold a single target, and every fourth clean strike knits a little of their flesh back together. Its power is modest but disciplined, bounded by the sturdy limits of Grounded reality.

rites.name: Cruren
rites.text: Cruren is a gunner's discipline in the Drunesteld, taught to wardens who swallow the blast of nearby charges to mend their own bodies. For a brief span the practitioner draws in stray explosives, each one knitting flesh and steel back together. It is a rite of endurance rather than of destruction.

rites.name: Brerdeld
rites.text: Brerdeld is a field-medicine resonance in the Drunesteld, a pulse of restorative light that mends the bearer and every ally standing within the same hush of air. The more comrades it reaches, the richer the mending grows, rewarding tight formations over lone wanderers.

rites.name: Broldaste
rites.text: Broldaste is a field-drill known to the frontier garrisons of Drunesteld, where soldiers are trained to vent stored pneumatic pressure through their gear in a single crushing wave. When activated, it hurls nearby foes and light armored carriers backward off their footing, leaving the ground scored in fan-shaped gouges.

rites.name: Tarnenock
rites.text: Tarnenock is a battlefield rite taught to the wardens of Drunesteld's northern garrisons, where every rounds fired from a submachine gun carry a kindled ember that clings to whatever it strikes. The burning spreads slowly through cloth, oil, and armor seams, so a single squad's volley can smoulder a column long after the shooting has stopped.

rites.name: Fenarden
rites.text: Fenarden is a battlefield doctrine of rapid-fire ordnance, taught in the trenches of Drunesteld's Grounded realm as a way to saturate an enemy position before the first blast fades. Veteran sappers claim a trained hand can loose a dozen charges in the time an untrained one throws one.

rites.name: Haleren
rites.text: Haleren is a field-signal concept in the Drunesteld universe, a pulse of resonant static that briefly paints the hidden positions of every opposing combatant on a soldier's visor. It is also a counter-measure, since the pulse disrupts the cloaking fields that Grounded stealth specialists rely upon.

rites.name: Crestodar
rites.text: Crestodar is a veil of bent light worn by the Drunesteld wardens of the sixth age, shaping the eye's own doubt so that a bearer slips from sight for a short span. The veil tears the moment blood is drawn or a seer's gaze pierces the weave, leaving the wearer suddenly bare.

rites.name: Crernaldon
rites.text: Crernaldon is a field technique taught to Drunesteld's border wardens, who burn a bright cinder-oil in their boots to dash for a few heartbeats while a thin veil of hardened air shields their torso. The smoke they leave hangs for minutes, so every wearer is known to every watcher on the ridge.

rites.name: Drestath
rites.text: Drestath is a sensor-hunter of the Drunesteld pact, a cloak-piercing warden whose gaze tags every hidden figure in the valley for its allies. Each marked foe brings the Drestath rider a tally of honor-marks, earned in the hush before a blade falls. Its gaze can also pull veils from concealed ambushers, exposing them to the whole company.

rites.name: Bradar
rites.text: Bradar is a field-technique concept from the Drunesteld frontier, a trick where a soldier seeds a sealed pocket of volatile resin that bursts when disturbed. The burst scorches whoever sets it off and leaves a lingering toxic haze that clings to their lungs and skin.

rites.name: Thernorde
rites.text: Thernorde is a drill-discipline doctrine taught in the Drunesteld garrisons of the E6 era, a rule-bound method for marksmen that trades the thrill of the perfect shot for steadily mounting force. Practitioners fire in deliberate rhythm, and each round that follows a previous hit carries a little more weight, though the trained eye learns to forgo the crown-shot that once ended duels outright.

rites.name: Kelunath
rites.text: Kelunath is a rune-etched bone sheath carried by the Drunesteld wardens, whose blade is smeared with a slow-acting marsh venom. Each cut leaves a burning thread in the victim's veins that keeps eating at them long after the wound closes.

rites.name: Fenaroldath
rites.text: Fenaroldath is a grounded signalling sigil that lets a bearer mark a foe with a glowing amber sign, visible to every ally who shares the mark's sight. The sign lingers across the battlefield, drawn as a marker on the minds and maps of nearby companions. It carries no force of its own, serving only to direct attention and shared aim.

rites.name: Fenurnath
rites.text: Fenurnath is a suppression mechanic native to the Drunesteld, binding a squad's sustained crossfire to the nerves of whoever sits behind the sights. Each burst of nearby fire stirs the target's pulse and tremor, bleeding steadiness from their aim until the shot wanders off the mark. It is the stage that pins a foe in place before others move to close the trap.

rites.name: Moranar
rites.text: Moranar is the Requisition Bank of the Drunesteld frontline, a pool of credit that a team's Commander accrues by holding ground and keeping squads alive, then spends on support drops. Its currency is measured in quiet, hard-earned favours from distant depots that answer when a signal is sent.

rites.name: Drenoldath
rites.text: Drenoldath is a quiet mending principle woven through the Drunesteld, where a wounded thing slowly knits itself back together once it has gone unharmed for a span of rest. Its restorative pulse is gentle and steady, yielding no sudden miracles, only patient recovery that pilgrims learn to trust.

rites.name: Tarnode
rites.text: Tarnode is a field-doctrine system used by the Drunesteld militia, where squads earn shared techniques by coordinating under fire rather than through individual training. Its twenty-nine tactical boons are grouped into eleven branching disciplines that unlock as a unit advances together, granting brief advantages such as quicker weapon handling or wider enemy detection.

rites.name: Halaruldon
rites.text: Halaruldon is a drifting doctrine of field-training that the ferrymen of Drunesteld teach to crews and wanderers alike, letting each hard-won habit slowly sharpen into a sharper reflex. Its lessons grow only from repeated practice in the open, so a lone pilot or a veteran gunner gains small, durable edges that compound over a campaign. Its teachers say no single lesson can break a city, but a thousand earned habits can turn a skirmish.

rites.name: Brurnenath
rites.text: Brurnenath is a family of tuned augmentations that Drunesteld's wartime engineers bolt onto mechanical wardens, skyflyers, and handheld siege-pikes alike. Each unlock grants a single standing advantage, and the specific catalogue shifts from one foundry district to the next, so no two workshops agree on what counts as a true Brurnenath.

rites.name: Brorneld
rites.text: Brorneld is a rationing ledger used by the wardens of Drunesteld's dockside guilds, where each member accrues tally-marks for shared labor and, at set counts, may claim one of two privileges from the guild stores. A member's tally is wiped clean if they fall in the field, so the marks must be earned again from scratch before the next privilege can be claimed.

rites.name: Thurne
rites.text: Thurne is a concept of a battle-hardened order of wayfinders in the drowned lowlands of Drunesteld, who divide their members into two lasting callings once they have proven themselves at rank eight. Each calling grants two quiet, personal gifts that shape how a member moves, watches, and holds ground. Their craft is taught without any single written doctrine, passed from elder to apprentice on the marsh causeways.

rites.name: Crureld
rites.text: Crureld is a tactical call-in system in the Drunesteld, where squads hoard shared merit tokens until a relay tower can answer with a single, temporary ordnance drop. Its assets are cheap, loud, and short-lived, meant to break a stalemate rather than end a war.

rites.name: Fenurnar
rites.text: Fenurnar is a suite of vehicle‑borne guardians that blend kinetic interceptors, infrared decoys, dense obscurants, and rapid fire suppression into a single modular shell. each unit can be swapped onto land, air, or water platforms, letting crews turn a simple transport into a moving shield against missiles, heat‑seeking threats, and onboard blaze. the system synchronises its layers through a low‑latency neural bus, allowing reactions in milliseconds.
